name: Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
history: The first Mass of the parish was said on Easter Sunday 1893 in a family home in Brooklyn's Sunset Park area; a wooden church followed in 1894. Construction of the present church began in 1907; the lower church opened in 1909 and the upper church was completed in 1928. Paul VI made it a basilica in 1969.
arch: A granite Romanesque church by Franz Joseph Untersee of Boston, with twin towers. Like the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi, it is a double church with two levels of worship.
features: It is staffed by the Redemptorists, who founded it.
Because of its size it hosts major diocesan services such as ordinations.

look.d: The towers rise over what was once called Irish Hill.
There are two churches here, one above the other.

fun: Memorial windows with Irish names recall the parish's early families.
journal: Two churches stacked like Assisi, on Brooklyn's old Irish Hill.
